key_insight: StableVQ argues that unstable VQ tokenizer training comes from the encoder-decoder and codebook being trained in a tightly coupled way. The paper’s key takeaway is that stability improves when each component is guided to do its own job more cleanly instead of relying on mutual compensation.
problem_solved: The paper addresses training instability in vector-quantized visual tokenizers, especially in shared-projection codebook methods where codebook utilization has improved but convergence and reliability remain difficult.
method: Analyzes the instability as an entanglement problem between encoder-decoder learning and codebook learning.
Proposes practical training guidelines to decouple responsibilities and stabilize optimization.
Focuses on improving consistent codebook usage while reducing training collapse and oscillation.
impact: This matters for practitioners building discrete image tokenizers for autoregressive and masked generative models, because stable training is essential for reliable performance and reproducibility. Better stability can reduce debugging time, improve codebook utilization, and make VQ-based pipelines more practical at scale.

paper_title: StableVQ: Practical Guidelines for Stable Vector-Quantized Tokenizer Training
paper_authors: Bao Tang, Jiahao Guo, Haoxiang Cao, Wenyu Liu, Changqian Yu
